_comment: ADIM 24 — DB round-trip budgets per operation. MEASURED, not aspirational.
The gate is backend/tests/integration/test_query_budgets.py; the methodology and
the fixed environment are docs/performance/README.md.
queries_small / queries_large are the TOTAL statements the operation issues at
n_small and n_large rows on its axis, from a cold identity map. per_item is the
slope between them and is the N+1 gate: a surface recorded at 0 that starts
reading per row fails even if its small-n total is unchanged.
This file is a RATCHET. Coming in under budget prints a tighten-me line naming
the new numbers (run with `pytest -s`); going over fails the build. Raising a
budget or a slope is a deliberate edit with a written reason in `note`, the same
idiom as frontend/e2e/a11y-baseline.json.
ONE HONEST BLIND SPOT, measured in P-E2 — do not read the slope as proving more
than it does. These are statement counts, so they cannot see a per-item
`session.get` for a PK a batch in the SAME session already loaded: the batch warms
SQLAlchemy's identity map and the read costs zero round trips. Measured: batch +
re-added per-item session.get = 2 statements, i.e. GREEN. The gate is not
under-reporting cost — that shape is genuinely free in production too, since the
command is one-tx-no-commit with expire_on_commit=False. What it cannot express is
the SMELL. It still catches every shape that costs anything: a per-item select()
(13 statements), a per-item read for an id the batch did not load (11 — identity-map
MISSES are never cached), and a batch that is removed or narrowed (12, slope 1).
Gating the smell itself needs a source-level assertion, not a counter.

measured_on.note: Counts are round trips, not wall-clock — identical on a laptop and on a GitHub runner, which is why this gate blocks PRs while the load run does not.

library.list_packages.title: Package Library — one catalog page (doc 08 §3)
library.list_packages.note: Flat. The viewer's share set, the joined catalog page, and ONE batched validatable-draft lookup. The per-row permission projection is computed in Python from rows already on the page — adding a per-row read here (a live rationale-family name, a per-row share check) is the regression this budget stops.

results_history.list_backtest_results.title: Results History — one index page (doc 16 §9.3)
results_history.list_backtest_results.note: Flat. Shared-composition ids, the visibility-filtered page, then three IN() batches (key-metric digests, immutable summaries, portfolio-mode markers). The markers batch exists precisely so the co-simulation era is not re-derived from each row's manifest — see queries/results_history.py::_load_portfolio_modes.

readiness_check.market_data_leg.title: Ready Check — market-data leg (doc 14 §9.2/§11)
readiness_check.market_data_leg.note: Flat since ADIM 46 (#617). Two batched reads: one IN() over the pinned market_dataset_revision ids (O-24b), then one IN() over the Roots those revisions name (market_repo.get_dataset_roots). The root batch is built AFTER the revision map because a Root is only reachable through the revision that pins it. Before the repair this row was a live N+1 — 12 statements at 11 Strategy items, a slope of 1 — because _resolve_market_data_issues called get_dataset_root INSIDE the item loop. Re-introducing any per-item read on the page a user waits on fails HERE, on the slope, even when the small-n total is unchanged.

readiness_check.signal_market_data_leg.title: Ready Check — Trading Signal OHLCV-fallback leg (doc 04 §5)
readiness_check.signal_market_data_leg.axis: Trading Signal item declaring an OHLCV fallback pin
readiness_check.signal_market_data_leg.note: Flat since P-E2. The THIRD instance of the #617 shape, and the one the earlier repair missed: _resolve_signal_market_data_issues already batched the pins (O-24b) and then called market_repo.get_dataset_root INSIDE the item loop. Two batched reads now: one IN() over the pinned market_dataset_revision ids, then one IN() over the Roots those revisions name (market_repo.get_dataset_roots, reused — no second idiom). Measured at 12 statements / slope 1 before the repair, so the leg cost one extra round trip per Trading Signal on the page a user waits on. test_readiness_query_count could not see it: that file filters on market_dataset_revision and the residual read was against entity_registry.

readiness_check.research_funding_leg.title: Ready Check — Research funding leg (doc 12 §9.2)
readiness_check.research_funding_leg.axis: Strategy item with an enabled funding source
readiness_check.research_funding_leg.note: Flat since P-E2. Same residual as the signal leg: _resolve_research_sources batched the funding pins and then dereferenced each resolved revision's Root in the loop. research_repo.get_dataset_roots is NEW here — the research repo had no plural reader, so it mirrors market_data.get_dataset_roots field for field (entity_type guard in SQL, absent == the per-id None). Measured at 12 statements / slope 1 before the repair. Only pins that RESOLVE reach the Root branch, so an unresolvable-feed fixture would measure a path the user never waits on — the test asserts every source is found.

readiness_check.tick_data_leg.title: Ready Check — tick-data availability leg (F-07i, Master Ref §6.4/§11.2)
readiness_check.tick_data_leg.axis: Strategy item requiring tick data ('Use Tick Data' = Yes)
readiness_check.tick_data_leg.note: Flat since P1. The FOURTH instance of the #617 shape: _resolve_tick_data_issues called market_repo.find_approved_tick_revision_for_instrument INSIDE `for item in items:`, one round trip per require-tick Strategy. Now one IN() read (market_repo.find_approved_tick_revisions_for_instruments, mirroring get_dataset_roots field for field), with _tick_data_demands collecting the require-tick items first. Measured at 1 -> 11 statements, slope 1, immediately before the repair. THE FIXTURE IS THE WHOLE MEASUREMENT HERE: the loop skips non-Strategy items, unavailable items, unparseable configs and — the narrow door — every strategy whose intrabar_policy.tick_policy is not 'require'. A fixture leaving the default 'inherit' measures 0 statements at BOTH sizes and reports a green slope of 0 for a leg that never ran; that was measured too, so this row's test flips the policy and asserts every item comes back BLOCKED. The batch picks the same row per instrument as the per-item reader: DISTINCT ON (instrument_id) over an ORDER BY whose per-item form was already TOTAL (created_at DESC, revision_id DESC), so there is no ordering ambiguity here — unlike leg 3, which stays unbatched behind gate G15.

readiness_check.strategy_mirror_leg.title: Ready Check - Strategy mirror deref (doc 02 7.1)
readiness_check.strategy_mirror_leg.axis: Strategy item pinning a doc-02 7.1 mirror revision
readiness_check.strategy_mirror_leg.note: FLAT, and measured that way (P2 / P-C2 Section D.1 leg 2). P4 (#754) added the seam - _mirror_ref, get_strategy_revisions and the optional `mirrors` parameter - but _build_item_inputs still called _resolve_strategy_payload WITHOUT a map, so Ready Check's mirror deref stayed per-item. P2 is that wiring: the refs are collected from the payloads the work-object batch already returned and dereferenced once. The two statements are those two batches and neither grows with the item count. Measured 2 at n=1 and 2 at n=11, slope 0.0. Every item gets its OWN mirror revision on purpose: items sharing one pin collapse to a single lookup and would stay flat even if the per-item deref came back. LIMIT OF THIS ROW, measured: restoring the per-item read while LEAVING the batch in place stays flat, because session.get on a PK the batch already warmed issues no SQL - the identity-map blind spot this file's header names. So this row catches a REMOVED batch, not a redundant read. Ratchet only. Leg 3 (_resolve_external) is NOT this row and stays per-item behind gate G15.

backtest_run.admission_tick_pins.title: RUN admission — pin the approved tick revision per tick-demanding Strategy (F-07i B, doc 15 §15)
backtest_run.admission_tick_pins.axis: tick-demanding Strategy item in the composition
backtest_run.admission_tick_pins.note: Flat since P4, and the FIRST budget row on the admission path: docs/performance/README.md §8 names 'Run admission' as the surface whose DB cost is gated deterministically instead of by the nightly load run, but no row here measured it, so it was entirely unmeasured. Measured at 3 -> 23, slope 2, immediately BEFORE the repair — commands/backtest_run.py::_resolve_tick_pins batched the pinned work-object revisions (O-24b) and then issued TWO reads inside `for entry in strategies:`: _resolve_strategy_payload's get_strategy_revision (the doc 02 §7.1 mirror deref) and find_approved_tick_revision_for_instrument. Now THREE batched reads: the work-object revisions, then the mirror pins those revisions name (strat_repo.get_strategy_revisions, NEW — mirrors mainboard.get_work_object_revisions field for field), then the instruments the resolved configs name (market_repo.find_approved_tick_revisions_for_instruments, REUSED from P1 — no second idiom). The order is load-bearing twice: a mirror ref is only reachable through the work-object revision carrying it, and an instrument only through the dereferenced config, which is why the tick probe cannot join the other two and the demands are collected first (the _tick_data_demands shape). NEITHER per-item read was the identity-map no-op this file's header describes, and that was measured rather than assumed: the header's GREEN case keeps the batch's result map alive, whereas _resolve_strategy_payload returns dict(revision.payload) and holds no reference, so the weakly-referenced StrategyRevision is collected and the next session.get is a real round trip — re-running the whole leg over a deliberately UN-expunged session reproduced the same slope of 2. THE FIXTURE IS LOAD-BEARING: this leg is FAIL-CLOSED, so the first tick-demanding strategy whose instrument has no approved revision raises 422 TICK_DATA_UNAVAILABLE and the remaining reads never fire — a blocked fixture would report a near-flat slope for a leg that stopped at item one. Every instrument here therefore HAS its own approved tick revision, and the test asserts the returned pin map names the expected revision for every item. WHICH row is pinned is not a performance detail: it enters the immutable manifest, so a batch that resolved a created_at tie differently would change the input replayed behind one execution_key (doc 15 §15, INF-04/INF-05). The per-instrument order was already TOTAL (created_at DESC, revision_id DESC), so DISTINCT ON cannot choose differently, and test_backtest_tick_pin_batch.py pins that against a deliberate equal-created_at tie.

dependency_pins.ensure_pinned_resolvers_.title: Approve Package — pinned ESP resolver re-validation (doc 06 §7)
dependency_pins.ensure_pinned_resolvers_.axis: pinned resolver ref on the revision
dependency_pins.ensure_pinned_resolvers_.note: Flat since ADIM 46 (#618). queries/dependency_pins.py::_prefetch issues one IN() over embedded_resolver_registry.canonical_key and then one over the revision ids those entries resolve to, and _pin_defect became a pure function over the two maps. The order is load-bearing: a ref that names no embedded_revision_id falls back to its entry's trusted_active_revision_id, so the revision batch is only knowable after the registry batch. Before the repair this was 22 statements at 11 pins, a slope of 2 — one registry read plus one revision read per ref, inside the loop.

agent_workspace.list_tasks.title: Analysis Lab — Alpha Agent task queue/history page (doc 18 §7)
agent_workspace.list_tasks.note: Flat: one keyset page, projected in Python. The cards carry no joined label today; this budget is what stops a later 'show each task's pinned context manifest' from arriving as a per-row read.

audit_log.list_audit_events.title: Admin — audit event page (M3 §8)
audit_log.list_audit_events.note: Flat, and a GUARD rather than a repair: the projection emits target_entity_id raw. Resolving a display label per row is the obvious next product request and the obvious next N+1 — it must arrive as one batched lookup, and this row is what forces that.

readiness_check.run_readiness_check.title: Ready Check — the WHOLE operation (doc 14 §9.2/§11)
readiness_check.run_readiness_check.axis: external work object item (trade_log / trading_signal) in the composition
readiness_check.run_readiness_check.note: NOT flat, and recorded that way on purpose (P3 / P-C2 §D.2). The per-leg rows above each measure one internal helper; growth that lives BETWEEN the legs is invisible to all of them, so this row measures run_readiness_check end to end and is the backstop for that gap. The slope is leg 3: _resolve_external (readiness_check.py:341) runs inside `for item, available in enabled:` and issues one resolve_trade_log_batch / resolve_signal_revision per external item. It is live and UNREPAIRED deliberately — batching it changes which row wins when two items pin the same work_object_revision_id, which is not UNIQUE, and that is an undecided product question (gate G15). P3 measures, it does not repair. The axis is the EXTERNAL kind because the cost is not uniform and both halves were measured: a strategy-only composition is FLAT at 9 statements (n=1 and n=11), since those items share one pinned package revision and the identity map absorbs the per-item read — the blind spot this file's header already names. Lowering per_item to 0 here would be a lie about the operation, not a repair of it. RE-MEASURED at P1 and UNMOVED (8 -> 18, slope 1): P1 batches the tick-data leg, which contributes zero statements to THIS fixture either way, because a trade_log composition has no Strategy item at all. Recorded because the reason matters — the 'strategy-only is FLAT at 9' half above held only because that fixture's strategies leave intrabar_policy.tick_policy at its 'inherit' default, so the tick leg never ran there. Measured directly at P1: the SAME leg over require-tick strategies was 1 -> 11, a slope of 1. A backstop row is only as wide as its fixture, and this one does not reach a leg whose door the composition never opens; that is what readiness_check.tick_data_leg is for.
